questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector With Respect to a Given Basis in a Polynomial Vector Space
questions.problem:
Consider the following polynomials:

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=1-3{t}^{2},\,{p}_{2}(t)=-3t+{t}^{2},\,q(t)=2-3t-5{t}^{2}.
$$

If $B={{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)},$ and $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)=q(t)
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(1-3{t}^{2})+{x}_{2}(-3t+{t}^{2}) & =2-3t-5{t}^{2} \\ {x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}t+(-3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}){t}^{2} & =2-3t-5{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=2 \\ -3{x}_{2}=-3 \\ -3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ -3 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ -3 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=2 \\ -3{x}_{2}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

From the first and second equations, we get ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=1.$ 

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=2+1=3.$

questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)+{x}_{3}{p}_{3}(t)=q(t).
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(-{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}-t)+{x}_{2}(3{t}^{3}+3t+18)+{x}_{3}({t}^{3}+{t}^{2}+t-9) & =-15{t}^{3}-2{t}^{2}-15t-9 \\ (-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}){t}^{3}+(3{x}_{1}+{x}_{3}){t}^{2}+(-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3})t+(18{x}_{2}-9{x}_{3}) & =-15{t}^{3}-2{t}^{2}-15t-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-15 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{3}=-2 \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-15 \\ 18{x}_{2}-9{x}_{3}=-9.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 1 & -15 \\ 3 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & -15 \\ 0 & 18 & -9 & -9\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 1 & -15 \\ 3 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & -15 \\ 0 & 18 & -9 & -9\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 1 & -15 \\ 0 & 9 & 4 & -47 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 18 & -9 & -9\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+(-2){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 1 & -15 \\ 0 & 9 & 4 & -47 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -17 & 85\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{3}↔{R}_{4} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 1 & -15 \\ 0 & 9 & 4 & -47 \\ 0 & 0 & -17 & 85 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-15 \\ 9{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=-47 \\ -17{x}_{3}=85.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-5.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
9{x}_{2}+4\cdot (-5)=-47\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-3.
$$

Now, substituting the obtained values into the first equation, we get

$$
-{x}_{1}+3\cdot (-3)+(-5)=-15\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=1.
$$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ -5\end{aligned}],$ and therefore ${x}_{1}=1.$

We need to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)+{x}_{3}{p}_{3}(t)=q(t).
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(-6{t}^{3}+6t+12)+{x}_{2}({t}^{3}-2{t}^{2}-3t-2)+{x}_{3}(-3{t}^{2}+2t) & =-9{t}^{3}+19t+18 \\ (-6{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}){t}^{3}+(-2{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}){t}^{2}+(6{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3})t+(12{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}) & =-9{t}^{3}+19t+18.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}-6{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-9 \\ -2{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 6{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=19 \\ 12{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=18.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-6 & 1 & 0 & -9 \\ 0 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 6 & -3 & 2 & 19 \\ 12 & -2 & 0 & 18\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}-6 & 1 & 0 & -9 \\ 0 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 6 & -3 & 2 & 19 \\ 12 & -2 & 0 & 18\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-6 & 1 & 0 & -9 \\ 0 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-6 & 1 & 0 & -9 \\ 0 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-6{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-9 \\ -2{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 5{x}_{3}=10.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
-2{x}_{2}-3\cdot 2=0\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-3.
$$

Now, substituting the obtained values into the first equation, we get

$$
-6{x}_{1}+(-3)=-9\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=1.
$$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ and therefore ${x}_{2}=-3.$

questions.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B={{B}_{1},{B}_{2}}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} & {x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1} & -3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{2}=1 \\ -2{x}_{1}=4 \\ -3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=8.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 & 4 \\ -3 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 & 4 \\ -3 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 6 & 6 \\ 0 & 11 & 11\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{2}=1 \\ 6{x}_{2}=6 \\ 11{x}_{2}=11.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second,  third and fourth equations, we get ${x}_{2}=1.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3\cdot 1 & =1 \\ {x}_{1} & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(-2)+1=-1.$

questions.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -8 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B={{B}_{1},{B}_{2}}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -8 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & -4{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -8 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-1 \\ -4{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=-8 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=7.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & -2 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & -2 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & 7\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 6 & -12 \\ 0 & -4 & 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-1 \\ 6{x}_{2}=-12 \\ -4{x}_{2}=8.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations, we get ${x}_{2}=-2.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2\cdot (-2) & =-1 \\ {x}_{1} & =-1+4 \\ {x}_{1} & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=3+(-2)=1.$
